headlines.title: Tesla reveals next-generation Roadster after almost a decade of delays
headlines.summary: Elon Musk first debuted the Roadster refresh concept in 2017 but Tesla has since missed every targeted delivery date.
headlines.article_text: Tesla Roadster reveal: What to know about the delayed EV Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Tesla revealed its next-generation Roadster from a SpaceX test site in Texas. CEO Elon Musk first debuted the Roadster refresh concept in 2017 but Tesla has since missed every targeted delivery date. Musk has promised fans a new Roadster with "rocket thrusters" that could "allow a Tesla to fly." In this article TSLA Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Tesla CEO Elon Musk during a state dinner in the East Room of the White House in Washington, Sept. 24, 2026. Annabelle Gordon | Bloomberg | Getty Images Tesla showed off its long-delayed next-generation Roadster on Thursday, almost a decade after Elon Musk's company started taking deposits for the electric sports car. The event was livestreamed from a SpaceX test site in McGregor, Texas, near Waco, starting at 7:55 p.m. local time, or 8:55 p.m. ET. In attendance along with Musk were design leader Franz von Holzhausen and Lars Moravy, vice president of vehicle engineering. "You're going to see some crazy stuff tonight," Musk said. "You're going to see the results of what happens when you have a collaboration with the world's best car company and the world's best rocket company." Tesla's original Roadster, designed and engineered by a team led by founding CEO Martin Eberhard, was based on a Lotus Elise chassis and was first delivered in 2008, selling for roughly $100,000 in small volumes until 2012. The next-generation Roadster is expected to be a high-end, low-volume model that relies on SpaceX technology, such as cold gas thrusters, to enable it to hover. Musk fanatics have been gearing up for the demonstration, expressing their excitement on social media, but the Roadster isn't likely to have any material financial impact on the company. At the event, Musk and his team showcased a white sports car that raced up a curved ramp, then hung upside down and vaulted off it, flipping in mid-air and hovering slowly before landing on the ground. The two-seater can go from zero to 60 miles per hour in under a second, according to Tesla's timer, a feat Moravy demonstrated for the live audience. Musk said the next-generation Roadster would enter production in 2028. The price wasn't announced. Tesla reopened reservations for the refreshed Roadster in recent weeks, accepting $50,000 deposits from prospective buyers in the U.S., Canada and China. Executives are expected to disclose specific pricing, details and production targets. Musk first promoted the refreshed Roadster concept at an event in November 2017 , and the following June in a series of tweets. He wrote at that time, "SpaceX option package for new Tesla Roadster will include ~10 small rocket thrusters arranged seamlessly around car." The engines would improve speed and braking, and may "even allow a Tesla to fly." Tesla started taking $50,000 deposits in 2017, but has since missed every targeted delivery date. As recently as last October, Musk was hyping a Roadster demo that he hoped would happen before the end of 2025. That didn't take place either. Musk's former friend and OpenAI co-founder Sam Altman mocked the Tesla CEO in posts on X last year over the extreme delays, showing screenshots of his own reservation and refund requests. "I really was excited for the car! And I understand delays," Altman wrote. "But 7.5 years has felt like a long time to wait." Altman got his refund, and the two ended up in court earlier this year over a separate matter related to OpenAI's governance and ownership structure. Others have kept their reservations. Lawrence O'Connor, founder and CEO of Other World Computing in Austin, Texas, told CNBC ahead of the event that he reserved a Founder's Edition of the new Roadster in November 2017, effectively giving the company what he called an "interest-free loan" of $250,000. O'Connor wrote in a message that he would be attending the show and was "excited to see what has been 9 years in the making." According to filings with the Federal Aviation Administration, Tesla established a no-fly zone around the SpaceX facility where it plans to show off the vehicle. The company had to scrap a demo on Oct. 1 due to weather issues. Tesla is scheduled to report third-quarter results after the bell on Wednesday. Andrew Harnik | Getty Images Technology giants Nvidia and Cisco have committed millions to President Donald Trump 's White House ballroom renovation project, CNBC confirmed on Thursday. Nvidia and Apple each pledged $25 million to the project, according to a report from The Washington Post . Those were among the largest donations on the list, which totaled more than $330 million. "As an American company, our support for the United States is paramount, and independent of any business interests," an Nvidia spokesperson told CNBC. "We were proud to be able to make a donation to a nonpartisan trust that serves all Americans and have said so publicly since the donation was made." Amazon , Palantir , ServiceNow , Meta Platforms and Microsoft also made contributions in the millions, according to the Post. Microsoft and Meta declined to comment on the report. Cisco and ServiceNow confirmed their $5 million donation. "ServiceNow's business with the U.S. government is separate and unconnected to any donations we make to any cause," the company said in a statement to CNBC. "Any attempt to connect the two processes is wholly inaccurate." Amazon, Apple, HP Inc. , Micron , Palantir, Salesforce and Vast Space, which were all listed as major donors in the report, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The Post reported that the ballroom donations were sent through a nonprofit trust, and donors received a pledge form for donating to the "Donald J. Trump Ballroom." Lawmakers and experts have repeatedly called out donations to the project, requesting information on the private donors. Some have also raised concerns over the potential influence these commitments could have on policy decisions or any federal contract awards. Tech leaders have largely favored Trump's pro-business, light-touch approach to antitrust and regulation, and some companies have secured hundreds of millions in contracts through artificial intelligence infrastructure and defense deals during his second term. Tech leaders like Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang have been regulars at state dinners and meetings in Washington, and were central figures at the White House AI luncheon on Sept. 29. headlines.summary: Signs of distressed deepened in CoreWeave on Thursday.
headlines.article_text: CoreWeave credit default swaps hit distress levels as investors sour on AI debt Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Signs of distressed deepened in CoreWeave on Thursday. Yields on its 2031 bonds topped 15%. Spreads in credit default swaps, which is insurance against defaults, widened to levels generally viewed as distressed. In this article CRWV Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Jonathan Raa | Nurphoto | Getty Images CoreWeave 's credit stress continued to spiral on Thursday amid a broader sell-off in AI-related names. CoreWeave — a so-called neocloud company — has taken on more than $51 billion of debt and obligations to finance its AI infrastructure build-out. It's now facing a rebellion from stock and bond investors as concerns mount about AI overspending and debt levels. Yields on CoreWeave debt have continued to climb, with the yield to maturity on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 reaching 15.78%. Bond yields move inversely to prices. Meanwhile, the spread on its five-year credit default swaps, which are insurance against default, at one point soared above 1,140 basis points. It last stood at nearly 1,038 bps — a 16% week-over-week jump and 164% higher than a year ago. Coreweave's 5-year credit default swap spread Credit concerns are spreading into AI equities too. CoreWeave's stock dropped during trading Thursday before recovering and closing 5.94% higher. The moved followed Wednesday's 15.5% nosedive . Other neocloud stocks were under similar pressure. Nebius also sank before climbing higher to close 1.29% and and Iren ultimately ended the day down less than 1%. Anxiety about AI overspending is also spreading. For instance, shares of Micron Technology and Advanced Micro Devices sold off following a big sell-off in South Korean chip stocks. Micron closed up 1.87%, while AMD fell 1.5%. While AI debt worries have been rising steadily, investors have suddenly grown skittish about the underlying finances of companies borrowing heavily to buy chips, build data centers, and rent out computing power. Coreweave's credit default swaps are one place to see that stress. Credit default swaps are contracts where buyers pay for protection in case the borrower can't repay its debt. The spread widening in CoreWeave's CDS means investors view the debt as riskier. The market is "basically saying 'no mas' to AI debt without operating cash flow support," the Evercore ISI trading desk said. A spread level of 1,000 basis points or above is generally a sign of credit distress, said Gavan Nolan, executive director of fixed income pricing at S&P Global Market Intelligence. CoreWeave's five-day performance No one is questioning whether demand for CoreWeave's services is real, since the company has contracts with all the big hyperscalers, Nolan said. The question is whether the cash flows will ultimately arrive. "It's obviously heavily negative free cash flow at the moment, and it needs that cash flow to arrive really to justify all the capex that it's spending," Nolan said. 'Self-fulfilling prophecy' CEO Mike Intrator dismissed the market moves on Wednesday, according to a memo obtained by CNBC. "When you are building a new type of technology company there will be periods of time when the market misunderstands and acts irrationally," he wrote. "We are confident in our backlog which more than supports all of our debt obligations." The backlog is over $100 billion, with around two-thirds of it with investment-grade counterparts including Microsoft , Meta , IBM and Caterpillar , Deutsche Bank said in a note Thursday. The firm reiterated its buy-rating on the stock Wednesday, calling the dislocation a buying opportunity. "The problem is this kind of concern can prove to be a self-fulfilling prophecy, and risks triggering broader issues in other AI-related names," said Jim Reid, global head of macro and thematic research. Oracle's 5-year credit default swaps spread Domino effects may already be happening. Oracle 's five-year CDS spread also spiked this week. It was last at 282 basis points, a roughly 10% increase in one week. "A downgrade from its BBB rating would risk pressuring IG-only investors into forced sales," Reid said.
